findings.title: Interpolating before the $__range split guard makes range-variable queries split incorrectly
findings.body: `querySupportsSplitting` intentionally excludes expressions containing range variables because their value must correspond to the unsplit request range. This change applies template variables before that check, so an expression such as `rate({app="api"}[$__range])` becomes a literal duration before `isQueryWithRangeVariable` runs and is no longer recognized as exempt. It will then be split into daily requests while retaining the duration calculated from the original full range, producing incorrect query windows and potentially duplicated or missing metric results. Preserve the pre-interpolation range-variable decision (or carry that metadata through interpolation) before partitioning.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expression are no longer filtered out
findings.body: The previous flow interpolated all targets and only then filtered out empty `expr` values. The new flow filters before `applyTemplateVariables`, so a target whose expression is a variable that resolves to an empty string is retained and passed into shard grouping and eventually query execution. This can send an invalid empty LogQL query instead of ignoring it; if it is the only target, it can also create a group where none should exist. Filter the interpolated `queries` collection for `query.expr` after mapping (and apply the same post-interpolation filtering in the time-splitting path).
